messages:
maria: Heads-up — CI started failing after we bumped tokenizers in the poetry lock (0.15.2 -> 0.16.0). KMS integration tests are flaking with native wheel load errors on the manylinux jobs. Anyone reproduced locally? @alex

alex: Yep reproduced on ubuntu-22 runner. Failure looks like: ImportError: /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libstdc++.so.6: undefined symbol: _ZSt7__cxx111 (or similar). Happens during `from tokenizers import Tokenizer` in our kms-signing tests.

jen: This smells like a wheel/ABI change in tokenizers 0.16.0 — they switched to a newer manylinux tag and dropped some compatibility. Short-term workaround: pin tokenizers==0.15.2 in the lockfile and add a restraint in our constraints file. Long-term we should either rebuild a compatible wheel in CI or upgrade the base image.

sam: Is there a security advisory attached? I scraped GH advisories and saw GHSA-xxxx-xxxx but couldn't confirm mapping to a CVE. If there's a CVE (e.g. CVE-2025-0421) we need to prioritize. Can someone confirm whether the advisory is about RCE/deserialization or just packaging/ABI?

security-oncall: Quick triage: CVE-2025-0421 (if that's the one) was about unsafe pickling in an older tokenizers helper — fixed in 0.16.1. If our code doesn't unpickle untrusted payloads it's lower risk, but since KMS signing touches serialized blobs we should assume medium risk until proven otherwise. Priority: P2 for now, escalate if exploitability is confirmed. Please capture audit logs around any failing sign/verify calls.

ci-bot: Job failure excerpt:
```
Task: test_kms_integration (e2e)
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File \"tests/e2e/test_kms_sign.py\", line 12, in <module>
    from tokenizers import Tokenizer
ImportError: /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libstdc++.so.6: undefined symbol: _ZSt7__cxx111

-- runner: ubuntu-22.04, python 3.11, manylinux2014 wheels not found for tokenizers 0.16.0
```

maria: Plan proposal: 1) Pin tokenizers==0.15.2 in poetry.lock + constraints and open a PR for release branches. 2) Add a CI matrix entry that forces manylinux2014 (current infra) to catch regressions. 3) If 0.16.x is required by transformers we coordinate with infra to upgrade base image or add a bundled wheel. I'll draft the PR: commands I ran locally to test pinning:

```bash
poetry add tokenizers==0.15.2 --lock
poetry lock --no-update
# run e2e tests locally in docker image matching CI
docker run --rm -v $PWD:/src -w /src python:3.11-bullseye bash -c \"pip install poetry && poetry install && pytest tests/e2e/test_kms_sign.py\"
```

alex: I'll take the backport PR to the 1.8.x branch and add the CI matrix change. Also will add a `wheelhouse/` fallback step in CI to prefer prebuilt wheels if compatibility mismatches show up.

jen: Also double-check transformers compatibility: some of our transformers pins expect tokenizers>=0.15.2. If we pin downwards we must run full model integration tests (embedding + generation smoke). I'll run a quick pass against the embeddings pipeline.

security-oncall: Actions for security tracking: create ticket SEC-2025-210 (sam can own), add audit log query to see any failed KMS sign attempts in the last 48h, and mark package pin as mitigation in the ticket. If we determine this is a packaging/ABI issue rather than a code vuln, note that in the advisory.

sam: Created SEC-2025-210 and linked PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/4321 (WIP). I'll attach CI failure artifacts and initial audit log query.

maria: Thanks all. I'll merge the pin PR into main once CI green on matrix, then open backport PRs to release branches. Will report back here when merged. :thumbsup:
